title: Editing fast
summary: F2, undo and redo, cut, copy, paste and Paste Special (values, formats, transpose).
objectives: Edit inside a cell with F2 instead of retyping it.
Undo and redo with the keyboard.
Use Paste Special for values, formats and transpose.

slides.h: Type over, or edit with F2
p: Click a cell and start typing: whatever was there is **replaced**. To fix one letter instead, press **F2** (or double-click): the cursor goes inside the cell and you can move with the arrow keys.
**Enter** finishes the edit, **Esc** cancels it, and **Delete** clears the cell’s contents but keeps its formatting.
**Ctrl+C** copies the selection; a moving dashed border shows what’s copied. Click where it should go and press **Ctrl+V**. Paste as many times as you like; press Esc to clear the border.
**Ctrl+X** cuts: the cells move to where you paste. Formulas that are copied adjust to their new place; you’ll see why in Module 6.

visual.text: Pressing **Enter** instead of Ctrl+V pastes once and clears the copy border.

check.q: Cell B3 says “Mumabi Central”. Quickest way to fix the typo?
options: Delete the cell and retype it all
Press F2 and fix the letters
check.explain: F2 puts you inside the cell so you can fix just the letters.

p: **Paste Special** (Ctrl+Alt+V, or right-click › Paste Special) lets you choose what to paste:
**Values** pastes results without formulas. **Formats** copies the look without the content. **Transpose** turns a row into a column, or a column into a row.

Paste **values** when you want to freeze results: sending a price list without your formulas, keeping a copy of this month’s totals before the data changes, or cleaning data imported from another system.
After pasting values, the cells hold plain numbers. Changing the inputs no longer changes them, which is the point.

bad.title: Plain paste of F2:F5
bad.text: The formulas come along and recalculate, pointing at new cells.

good.title: Paste values
good.text: Only the numbers arrive. Nothing recalculates.

check.q: You need a copy of the totals that won’t change when the data changes. Which paste?
check.explain: Values pastes results, without the formulas behind them.
